design_gotchas.title: INVERTED LOGIC: Pin 5 (ON/OFF) Is ACTIVE-LOW Enable (Opposite of Modern Bucks!)
design_gotchas.detail: Pulling Pin 5 (ON/OFF) below 1.3 V (grounded or open) turns LM2596 ON, whereas pulling it above 1.3 V (up to 25 V max) SHUTS IT DOWN. This polarity is inverted compared to TPS54302DDCR, TPS54331DR, AP63203WU-7, and AP62200WU-7.

design_gotchas.title: Non-Synchronous Bipolar NPN Switch (VSAT = 1.16 V) Limits Efficiency to ~80% & Needs Copper Heatsinking
design_gotchas.detail: Because LM2596 uses a legacy Darlington/bipolar switch (~1.16 V typ / 1.5 V max saturation at 3 A) plus an external Schottky diode, full 3 A load dissipates ~2.5-3.5 W across IC and diode (~80% efficiency vs 92-95% on synchronous MOSFET bucks). Large PCB copper area on the GND tab (<= 30°C/W) is mandatory at 3 A.

design_gotchas.title: Legacy 150 kHz Frequency Demands Bulky 33-47 uH Inductors & Finite-ESR Electrolytic Capacitors
design_gotchas.detail: At 150 kHz, LM2596 requires large 33-47 uH inductors and 82-330 uF low-ESR electrolytic or tantalum output capacitors whose ESR provides loop zero damping. Pure ultra-low-ESR MLCC ceramic capacitors on input/output can trigger severe ringing (p.26) or loop instability.

design_gotchas.title: High 5 mA Operating Iq and 7 V Minimum Input for 5 V Regulation
design_gotchas.detail: LM2596SX-5.0/NOPB draws 5 mA typical quiescent current (100x higher than TPS54302's 45 uA) and needs at least 7.0 V input (2 V headroom) to regulate 5.0 V accurately at 3 A, though it uniquely handles up to 40 V continuous (45 V abs max) industrial buses.

typical_use_cases: Legacy 24 V to 40 V industrial control, telecom, and automotive-adjacent step-down to fixed 5.0 V at up to 3 A
Rugged high-voltage pre-regulator for linear LDOs where 40 V continuous input tolerance outweighs board space
Reference baseline when migrating bulky 150 kHz TO-263 designs to modern compact 28-32 V synchronous MOSFET bucks
engineering_summary: The LM2596SX-5.0/NOPB is a classic SIMPLE SWITCHER 150 kHz non-synchronous bipolar buck regulator in a 5-pin TO-263 (KTT / DDPAK) power package (GND metal tab, RthetaJA = 20-50°C/W) delivering fixed 5.0 V at 3 A from wide 7.0 V to 40 V inputs (45 V abs max). Compared to modern synchronous bucks like TPS54302DDCR or AP63203WU-7, it tolerates higher 40 V inputs but suffers ~80% efficiency, 5 mA quiescent current, bulky 33-47 uH inductors, finite-ESR electrolytic capacitor requirements, and inverted ACTIVE-LOW ON/OFF enable polarity. Verify copper heatsinking and capacitor ESR stability in the TI datasheet before production.

audit_notes: 300 DPI PNG Vision inspection on p.4 Fig 6-2 confirmed KTT 5-pin TO-263 (DDPAK) Top View pinout (1=VIN, 2=Output, 3=Ground, 4=Feedback, 5=ON/OFF) with metal thermal tab internally connected to Ground.

300 DPI PNG Vision inspection on p.5 verified Abs Max VIN 45 V, ON/OFF 25 V, Rec Op VIN 4.5-40 V (7-40 V for 5 V version p.6), TJ -40 to 125 C, RthetaJA 50 C/W (0.5 sq-in Cu; 30/20 C/W larger Cu), and RthetaJC 2 C/W.
Confirmed inverted ACTIVE-LOW ON/OFF enable polarity (en_active_high: false), 150 kHz oscillator, 5 mA Iq, 80% efficiency at 12 V -> 5 V / 3 A, and electrolytic/tantalum ESR requirements.
